therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: synaptic vesicle release modulation / neuronal hyperactivity suppression
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: hippocampal circuit normalization / reduction of dentate gyrus-CA3 hyperactivity
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adults with amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI)
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Brain activity in the dentate gyrus / CA3 subregion of the hippocampus measured with BOLD fMRI

results.effect_size: At 125mg BID: DG/CA3 BOLD mean beta = -0.2238 (drug) vs 0.8814 (placebo); at 62.5mg BID: -0.1203 (drug) vs 0.4353 (placebo); at 250mg BID: 0.3928 (drug) vs 0.4825 (placebo); age-matched controls: -0.02507
results.target_engagement_evidence: Reduction in DG/CA3 BOLD signal toward control levels at 62.5mg and 125mg doses, consistent with suppression of hippocampal hyperactivity
biomarker_changes: DG/CA3 BOLD mean beta reduced from 0.4353 (placebo) to -0.1203 (drug) at 62.5mg BID
DG/CA3 BOLD mean beta reduced from 0.8814 (placebo) to -0.2238 (drug) at 125mg BID
DG/CA3 BOLD mean beta minimally changed from 0.4825 (placebo) to 0.3928 (drug) at 250mg BID
Age-matched controls showed DG/CA3 BOLD mean beta of -0.02507

dose_info.schedule: twice daily for 2 weeks per period (crossover)

context.investigator_commentary: The trial used a crossover design with three levetiracetam doses (62.5mg, 125mg, 250mg BID) compared to placebo in aMCI patients, with age-matched controls as a reference group. The 125mg BID dose showed the greatest reduction in DG/CA3 hyperactivity toward control levels, suggesting an inverted-U dose-response relationship.
